Background

In the data folder, you will find data about shark incidents in California between 1950-2022. The data are from: State of California- Shark Incident Database.

Load the libraries

library("tidyverse")
library("janitor")

Load the data

Run the following code chunk to import the data. In this chunk, I am removing NA’s.

sharks <- 
  read_csv("data/SharkIncidents_1950_2022_220302.csv", 
           na=c("NA", "N/A", "Unknown", "NOT COUNTED", "", " ")) %>% 
  clean_names()

Questions

  1. Are there any “hotspots” for shark incidents in California? Show the top five counties with the most incidents.
sharks %>%
  group_by(county) %>%
  summarize(n_incidents = n()) %>%
  slice_max(n_incidents, n=5)
## # A tibble: 6 × 2
##   county        n_incidents
##   <chr>               <int>
## 1 San Diego              25
## 2 Humboldt               20
## 3 San Mateo              19
## 4 Santa Barbara          19
## 5 Marin                  16
## 6 Monterey               16
  1. Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents per county.
sharks %>%
  group_by(county) %>%
  summarize(n = n()) %>%
  ggplot(mapping=aes(x=reorder(county, n), y=n))+
  geom_col(color="black", fill="lemonchiffon", na.rm=T)+
  coord_flip()+
  labs(x="County", y=NULL, title="CA: Number of Shark Incidents by County")+
  theme(plot.title=element_text(size=rel(1.3), hjust=0.5))

  1. Are there months of the year when incidents are more likely to occur? Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by month. Which month has the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarize(n_incidents = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_incidents))
## # A tibble: 12 × 2
##    month n_incidents
##    <dbl>       <int>
##  1    10          36
##  2     9          34
##  3     8          31
##  4     7          27
##  5     5          16
##  6    11          16
##  7     6          14
##  8    12          13
##  9     1           8
## 10     4           7
## 11     3           5
## 12     2           4
#Yes, there are months when incidents are more likely to occur.
sharks %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarize(n = n()) %>%
  ggplot(mapping=aes(x=reorder(month, n), y=n))+
  geom_col(color="black", fill="lightgreen", na.rm=T)+
  coord_flip()+
  labs(x="Month", y=NULL, title="CA: Number of Shark Incidents by Month")+
  theme(plot.title=element_text(size=rel(1.3), hjust=0.5))

#October has the highest number of shark incidents.
  1. Is there a time of day when most attacks occur? Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by time of day. Which time of day has the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>%
  filter(time != "NA") %>%
  group_by(time) %>%
  summarize(n_incidents = n()) %>%
  slice_max(n_incidents)
## # A tibble: 1 × 2
##   time  n_incidents
##   <chr>       <int>
## 1 11:00          18
sharks %>%
  filter(time != "NA") %>%
  group_by(time) %>%
  summarize(n = n()) %>%
  ggplot(mapping=aes(x=reorder(time, n), y=n))+
  geom_col(color="black", fill="rosybrown2", na.rm=T)+
  labs(x="Time of Day",
       y=NULL,
       title="CA: Number of Shark Incidents by Time of Day")+
  coord_flip()+
  theme(plot.title=element_text(size=rel(1.3), hjust=0.5),
        axis.text.y=element_text(size=rel(0.75)))

#11:00 a.m. is most common for shark attacks.
  1. How do the number and types of injuries compare by county? Make a table that shows the number of injury types by county. Which county has the highest number incidents? (hint: your table should be in wide format)
#Number of injury types by county
sharks %>%
  group_by(county) %>%
  summarize(n_injury_types = n_distinct(injury, na.rm=T)) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_injury_types))

#San Diego County has the highest number of injury types.
#San Diego County also has the highest number of incidents (question is unclear & seems to be a repeat of question 1).
  1. Use the table from #5 to make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by county.
#The question seems to be a repeat of question 2 but I don't think that's what's meant.
#So here is number of incidents by injury type & county.
sharks %>%
  group_by(county, injury) %>%
  summarize(n = n(), .groups="keep") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = "injury",
              values_from = "n") %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  pivot_longer(-county,
               names_to = "injury",
               values_to = "n_incidents") %>%
  na.omit %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=county, y=n_incidents, fill=injury))+
  geom_col(position="dodge", na.rm=T)+
  coord_flip()+
  labs(x="County", y=NULL, title="CA: Number of Shark Incidents by County & Type")+
  theme(plot.title=element_text(size=rel(1.3), hjust=0.5))

  1. In the data, mode refers to a type of activity. Which activity is associated with the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>%
  group_by(mode) %>%
  summarize(n_incidents = n()) %>%
  slice_max(n_incidents)
## # A tibble: 1 × 2
##   mode               n_incidents
##   <chr>                    <int>
## 1 Surfing / Boarding          85
  1. Make a plot that compares the number of incidents by activity.
sharks %>%
  group_by(mode) %>%
  summarize(n_incidents = n()) %>%
  ggplot(mapping=aes(x=reorder(mode, n_incidents), y=n_incidents))+
  geom_col(color="black", fill="lightblue2", na.rm=T)+
  coord_flip()+
  labs(x="Activity", y=NULL, title="CA: Number of Shark Incidents by Human Activity")+
  theme(plot.title=element_text(size=rel(1.3), hjust=0.5))

  1. Which shark species is involved in the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarize(n_incidents = n()) %>%
  slice_max(n_incidents)
## # A tibble: 1 × 2
##   species n_incidents
##   <chr>         <int>
## 1 White           181
#Great White Sharks
  1. Are all incidents involving Great White’s fatal? Make a plot that shows the number and types of incidents for Great White’s only.
sharks %>%
  filter(species == "White") %>%
  group_by(injury) %>%
  summarize(n_incidents = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_incidents))
## # A tibble: 5 × 2
##   injury n_incidents
##   <chr>        <int>
## 1 none            74
## 2 major           59
## 3 minor           31
## 4 fatal           15
## 5 none*            2
#No, the majority of Great White incidents resulted in no injury.
sharks %>%
  filter(species == "White") %>%
  group_by(injury) %>%
  summarize(n = n()) %>%
  ggplot(mapping=aes(x=reorder(injury, n), y=n))+
  geom_col(color="black", fill="skyblue", na.rm=T) +
  coord_flip()+
  labs(x="Injury Type", y=NULL,
       title="CA: Count of Injury Types from Great White Shark Incidents")+
  theme(plot.title=element_text(size=rel(1.3), hjust=0.5))
